content.html: Conduct of an Audit in Accordance with Standards on Auditing
Overall Objective of Auditor?
In conducting audit of FS, overall objectives of auditor are:
To obtain Reasonable Assurance about whether FS are free from material misstatement, whether due
to fraud or error, to express opinion whether FS are prepared, in all material respects, as per AFRF &
To report & communicate as per SAs.
Definitions
Reasonable Assurance: High, but not absolute, level of assurance.
To obtain reasonable assurance, obtain Sufficient & Appropriate Audit Evidence (SAAE).
v
v
v
v
Sufficiency is measure of quantity of audit evidence affected by ROMM & Quality of audit evidence.
Appropriateness is measure of Quality of audit evidence i.e. its relevance & its reliability.
Relevance is the logical connection between the purpose of audit procedure & assertion tested.
Reliablity depends on nature, source & circumstances in which audit evidence is obtained.
o Reliability increased when obtained from independent sources outside entity.
o Reliability of A.E. generated internally is increased when related controls are effective.
AE. obtained directly by auditor more reliable than A.E. obtained indirectly or by inference.
A.E. in documentary form more reliable than evidence obtained orally.
A.E. provided by original documents more reliable than photocopies or digitised.
oo°0
Misstatement: Difference between amount, classification, presentation, or disclosure (a/c/p/d) of a
reported FS item & (a/c/p/d) required as per AFRF. Misstatements can arise from error or fraud.
Misstatement considered material if it can influence economic decisions of user of FS.
Applicable financial reporting framework (AFRF):
FRF adopted by mgt & TCWG in preparation & presentation of FS that's acceptable in view of nature of
entity & objective of FS or required by law or regulation.
“Fair presentation framework" refer to FRF that requires compliance with framework &
i)
Acknowledges, to provide disclosures beyond specifically required by framework or
ii) Necessary to depart from framework to achieve fair presentation in extremely rare circumstances.
“Compliance framework" is FRF that requires compliance with framework, but doesn't contain
acknowledgements in (i) or (ii) above.
Assertions (SA 315):
Representations by mgt embodied in FS, used by auditor to consider different potential misstatements.
Classes of transactions and events: Occurrence, Completeness, Accuracy, Cut-off, Classification
Account Balance: Existence, Rights & obligations, Completeness & Valuation
Presentation & Disclosure: Mix of above (excluding cut-off & existence)

entity & obligations related to accountability of entity. (Audit committee/CFO/Chairman)
Audit Risk
Risk that auditor expresses inappropriate audit opinion when FS are materially misstated.
Audit risk is function of RoMM and detection risk.
Risk of material misstatement (ROMM): Risk that FS are materially misstated prior to audit. This
consists of 2 components, described as follows at assertion level:
Inherent Risk Control Risk
Susceptibility of an assertion about a ABCD Risk that misstatement that could occur in an
to a misstatement that could be material, assertion about a ABCD & could be material
(individually or when aggregated with other (individually or when aggregated with other
misstatements), before consideration of misstatements) will not be prevented, or detected
any related controls. & corrected, on timely basis by internal control.
ROMM may exist at two levels:
Overall F.S. level i.e. relate to FS as a whole Assertion level for A/c balances, Class of
affecting many assertions Transactions, and disclosures (ABCD)
Why we assess RoMM at assertion level?
ROMM at assertion level assessed to determine NTE of FAP to obtain SAAE.
Detection risk: Risk that procedures performed by auditor will not detect a misstatement that exists &
could be material (individually or when aggregated with other misstatements).
Inherent Limitations of Audit (ILA)
Auditor isn't expected & can't reduce audit risk to zero & therefore can't obtain absolute assurance that
FS are free from material misstatement due to fraud or error. This is because of inherent limitations
of audit, which result in most audit evidence being persuasive rather than conclusive.
1. Nature of financial reporting:
Preparation of FS involves judgment by mgt in applying requirements of AFRF to facts & circumstances
of entity. For eg: A/c estimates
2. Nature of audit procedures:
¢ Possibility that mgt & others don't provide complete info relevant to preparation of FS

* Audit is not official investigation. He doesn't have special legal powers eg. search.

content.html: Objective

Establishing whether preconditions for audit are present &
Confirming common understanding between auditor & mgt , TCWG of terms of audit engg.
Preconditions of Audit
Determine whether FRF is acceptable [Factors discussed below]
Obtain agreement of mgt that it acknowledges & understands its responsibility:
i) For preparation of FS as per AFRF
ii) For such Internal Control (IC) to prepare FS free from material misstatement, due to fraud or error &
iii) To provide auditor with:

b) Additional info. that auditor may request for audit &
c) Unrestricted access to persons within entity to obtain audit evidence.
Tf preconditions not present, discuss with mgt & do not accept proposed audit.
Factors relevant to auditor's determination of acceptability of FRF to be applied in preparation of FS include:
Nature of entity (business enterprise or not for profit organization)
Purpose of FS (prepared to meet common financial info. needs of wide range of users or specific users)
Nature of FS (complete set of FS or single FS)
Whether law or regulation prescribes AFRF.

Acceptance of Change in Terms of Audit Engagement
Auditor shall not agree to change in terms of audit engg. where there is no reasonable justification for doing so.
v If prior to completing audit, auditor is requested to change it to engg. that conveys lower level of assurance,

Tf auditor unable to agree to change of terms & not permitted by mgt to continue:
Withdraw from audit engg. where possible under law or regulation &
b. Determine whether obligation to report to other parties, such as TCWG, owners or regulators
Recurring Audits: New engagement letter each time?
Auditor may decide not to send new audit engg. letter or other written agreement each period.
Following factors make it appropriate to revise terms of audit engg. or remind entity of existing terms:
Entity misunderstands objective & scope of audit. Revised or special terms of audit engg.
Recent change of senior mgt. Significant change in ownership.
Significant change in nature or size of business. Change in legal or regulatory requirements.
Change in FRF adopted in preparation of FS. Change in other reporting requirements.

topics.title: SA 240: Auditor's Responsibilities relating to Fraud

content.html: in an Audit of FS.
Assist auditor in identifying & assessing RoMM due to fraud & procedures to detect such misstatement.
Objectives of auditor
a) To identify & assess RoMM in FS due to fraud
b) To obtain SAAE about assessed RoMM due to fraud, through designing & implementing responses &
c) To respond appropriately to identified or suspected fraud.
Fraudulent Financial Reporting (FFR) Misappropriation of assets
Intentional misstatements in FS to deceive FS | Theft of entity's assets & often done by employees
users by mgt. in relatively small & immaterial amounts
Fraudulent financial reporting may be accomplished by:
i. Manipulation, falsification (including forgery), or alteration of a/c records or supporting documentation
from which FS are prepared.
ii, Misrepresentation or intentional omission from FS of events, transactions or other significant info.
iii. Intentional misapplication of a/c principles relating to amts, classification, manner of presentation, or
disclosure.
It often involves mgt override of controls that otherwise may appear to be operating effectively.
Fraud can be committed by mgt overriding controls using such techniques as:
i) Altering records and terms related to Significant and unusual transactions,
ii) Recording Fictitious journal entries, close to end of a/c period, to manipulate operating results.
iii) Inappropriately Adjusting Assumptions & changing judgments used to estimate a/c balances.
iv) Concealing, or not disclosing, facts that could affect amounts recorded in F.S.
v) Engaging in Complex transactions to misrepresent financial position or performance of entity.
vi) Omitting, advancing or delaying recognition of events & Transactions in FS occurred during period.

Techniques of Misappropriation of Assets
i) Embezzling receipts (misappropriating collections from debtors)
ii) Stealing physical assets or intellectual property (stealing inventory for personal use/sale)
iii) Causing entity to pay for goods & services not received (payments to fictitious vendors/employees)
iv) Using entity's assets for personal use (as collateral for a personal loan or a loan to a related party).
Primary responsibility to prevent & detect fraud > Mgt & TCWG
Auditor Responsibility?
Auditor is responsible for obtaining RA that FS are free from MM due to fraud/error.
© Owing to ILA, there is unavoidable risk that some MM may not be detected, even though audit planned
& performed as per SAs. Potential effects of ILA are significant for fraud.
Risk of not detecting a MM from fraud is higher than error. Because fraud may involve sophisticated
& carefully organized schemes designed to conceal it.
© Further, risk of not detecting MM from mgt fraud is greater than employee fraud, because mgt is ina
position to directly/indirectly manipulate a/c records, present fraudulent financial info. or override
control procedures to prevent similar frauds by other employees.
e When obtaining RA, auditor is responsible for maintaining professional skepticism, considering potential
for mgt override of controls & recognizing that audit procedures effective for detecting error may
not be effective in detecting fraud.
e Auditor may accept records & documents as genuine.
e If auditor believes document may not be authentic or modified, investigate further.
© Where responses to inquiries of mgt or TCWG are inconsistent, investigate the inconsistencies.
What are fraud risk factors?
Events or conditions that indicate incentive or pressure or provide opportunity to commit fraud.
Examples:
e Pressure: Need to meet expectations of 3" parties to obtain additional equity financing
© Incentive: Granting of significant bonuses if unrealistic profit targets are met &
© Opportunity: Control environment that is not effective.

topics.title: SA 250: Consideration of Laws & Regulations in an Audit of FS

content.html: Assist auditor in identifying MM in FS due to Non-compliance with laws & regulations (NOCLAR).
Objectives of auditor
To obtain SAAE regarding compliance with those L&Rs having direct effect on determining material
amounts & disclosures in FS
To perform specified audit procedures to identify instances of non-compliance with other laws &
regulations that may have a material effect on FS &
To respond appropriately to non-compliance or suspected non-compliance with laws & regulations
identified during audit.
Mgt Responsibility for compliance with L&Rs
Following are procedures entity implement to assist in prevention & detection of NOCLAR:
Monitoring legal requirements & ensuring operating procedures designed to meet these requirements.
Instituting & operating systems of internal control,
Developing, publicising & following a code of conduct.
Ensuring employees are trained & understand code of conduct.
Monitoring compliance with code of conduct & discipline employees who fail to comply with it.
Engaging legal advisors to assist in monitoring legal requirements.
Maintaining register of significant applicable L&Rs & record of complaints.
Auditor's responsibility in relation to Compliance with Laws & Regulations (L/Rs)
Auditor responsible for obtaining reasonable assurance that FS are free from material misstatement,
due to fraud/error. Auditor considers applicable legal & regulatory framework.
Owing to inherent limitations of audit, there is unavoidable risk that some MM may not be detected,
even though audit planned & performed as per SAs
In context of L/Rs, potential effects of inherent limitations on auditor's ability to detect MM are
greater for such reasons as following: - >
There are many laws & regulations, relating to operating aspects of entity that typically don't affect
FS & not captured by entity's info. systems relevant to financial reporting.
Non-compliance may involve conduct designed to conceal it, such as collusion, forgery, etc.
Whether act is a non-compliance is ultimately matter for legal determination by court of law.
2 Types of L/Rs
Auditor's responsibilities in relation to compliance with 2 different categories of L&Rs:
Provisions of those LARs having direct effect on determination of material amounts & disclosures in FS

Effective 2-way communication is important in assisting:

topics.title: SA 265 “Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control to TCWG & Mgt"

content.html: Auditor's Objective
To communicate to TCWG & mgt, deficiencies in IC that auditor identified & in auditor's professional
judgment of sufficient importance to merit their respective attentions.
Deficiency in IC:
i) Control designed, implemented or operated in a way it's unable to Prevent/Detect/Correct,
misstatements in FS on a timely basis or
ii) A control necessary to P/D/C misstatements in FS ona timely basis is missing.
Significant deficiency in IC: Deficiency or combination of deficiencies in IC, in auditor's professional
judgment, of sufficient importance to merit attention of TCWG.
Note: Significance of a deficiency(s) in internal control depends not only on whether a misstatement
has actually occurred, but also on likelihood & potential magnitude of misstatement.
Significant deficiencies may exist even though auditor has not identified misstatements during audit.
Requirements
» Determine whether, on basis of work performed, he has identified one or more deficiencies in TC;
> If identified one or more deficiencies in IC, determine, on basis of work performed, whether, individually
or in combination, they constitute significant deficiencies.
> Auditor shall communicate in writing significant deficiencies in IC to TCWG ona timely basis.
» Auditor shall also communicate to mgt at an appropriate level of responsibility on a timely basis:
a. In writing, significant deficiencies in IC that auditor has communicated or intends to communicate
to TCWG, unless it would be inappropriate to communicate directly to mgt in circumstances &
b. Other deficiencies in IC that haven't been communicated to mgt by other parties & are of sufficient
importance to merit mgt's attention.
Written communication to TCWG
Auditor shall include in written communication of significant deficiencies in internal control:
a. Description of deficiencies & explanation of their potential effects &
b. Sufficient info. to enable TCWG & mgt understand context of communication.

topics.title: SA 299 “Joint Audit of FS"

content.html: Joint audit is audit of FS by 2 or more auditors, Such auditors are called joint auditors.
For eg, Sec 139(3) of Companies Act, 2013 provides that members of a Co, may resolve to provide that
audit shall be conducted by more than one auditor.
Audit Planning, Risk Assessment and Allocation of Work
EP & other key members of team from each of joint auditors involved in planning.
Joint auditors jointly establish overall audit strategy that sets scope, timing & direction of audit, &
guides development of audit plan.
Prior to commencement of audit, joint auditors discuss & develop a joint audit plan.
In developing joint audit plan, joint auditors shall:
Identify division of audit areas & common audit areas that define scope of work of each joint auditor
Joint auditors should, divide audit work. Usually in terms of audit of identifiable units or specified areas.
In some cases, due to nature of business, such division may not be possible.
In such cases, division maybe w.r.t items of assets/liabilities/income/expenditure.
Certain areas of work, may not be divided & covered by all joint auditors.
Ascertain reporting objectives of engagement to plan timing of audit & nature of communications
Communicate among all joint auditors factors significant in directing engagement team's efforts
Consider results of preliminary engagement activities & knowledge gained on other engagements
Ascertain NTE of resources necessary to perform engagement
At this stage, ROMM assessed by each joint auditor & communicated to other joint auditors &
documented, whether pertaining to overall FS level or area of allocation among other joint auditors.
Joint auditors discuss & document NTE of audit procedures for common & specific allotted areas &
communicate to TCWG.
Joint auditors shall obtain common Engg Letter & common mgt representation letter.
Work allocation document shall be signed by all joint auditors & communicated to TCWG.
Responsibility and Co-ordination among Joint Auditors
In respect of audit work divided, each joint auditor responsible only for work allocated.
All the joint auditors shall be jointly & severally responsible for:
a. audit work not divided among joint auditors & carried by all joint auditors
b. decisions taken by all joint auditors under audit planning for common areas concerning NTE of
procedures to be performed by each Joint Auditor [Execution > Individual Responsibility]
. matters brought to notice by any one of them & on which there is agreement among all
. examining that FS comply with relevant statutes

topics.title: SA 320: Materiality in Planning & Performing an Audit

content.html: Determining Materiality & Performance Materiality when planning Audit
When establishing overall audit strategy, determine materiality for FS as whole.
o If, there's one or more particular ABCD for which misstatements of lesser amounts than materiality
for FS as whole could influence economic decisions of users taken on basis of FS, also determine
materiality level(s) for those particular ABCD.
o Determine performance materiality for assessing ROMM & determining NTE of FAP.
Performance Materiality (PM) means
© amount or amounts set by auditor at less than materiality for F.S. as whole
© to reduce probability that aggregate of uncorrected & undetected misstatements
o exceeds materiality for FS as a whole.
If applicable, PM also refers to amt or amounts set by auditor at less than materiality level or levels for
particular ABCD.
Benchmark 7
Determining materiality involves exercise of professional judgment. A percentage is applied to chosen
benchmark as starting point in determining materiality for FS as whole.
Factors that affect identification of appropriate benchmark include following:
v Elements of FS (for eg, assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses)
vy Whether there are items on which attention of users of particular entity's FS tends to be focused (for
eg, for evaluating financial performance users may focus on profit, revenue or net assets)
v Nature of entity, where entity is in its life cycle, industry & economic environment
vy Entity's ownership structure & way it is financed (for eg, if entity is financed solely by debt rather than
equity, users may put more emphasis on assets, & claims on them, than on entity's earnings) &
v_ Relative volatility of benchmark.
Element of FS >> Focus >> Ownership structure >> Life cycle >> Volatility
Note: There is relationship between age & chosen benchmark, such that a percentage applied to PBT
from continuing operations will normally be higher than %age applied to total revenue.
Examples of benchmarks include categories of reported income such as profit before tax, total revenue,
gross profit, total expenses, total equity or net asset value.
Type of entity & benchmark
Profit oriented > Profit before tax Public utility projects: Total or Net costs
If PBT Volatile : Gross Profit or Total Revenues | Custody of assets: Assets
Revision of Materiality
Revise materiality for FS as a whole (& if applicable, materiality level for particular ABCD) in event of
becoming aware of info.* during audit that would have caused auditor to have determined different
amount initially,
* may need to be revised as a result of
a, change in circumstances during audit (for eg, decision to dispose of major part of business),
b. new information, or
¢c. change in auditor's understanding of entity & its operations as a result of FAP.
For eg, if actual financial results are substantially different from anticipated period end financial
results that were used initially to determine materiality for FS, auditor revises that materiality.
If auditor concludes lower materiality for FS as whole (&, if applicable, materiality level(s) for
particular ABCD) than initially determined, determine whether necessary to revise Performance
Materiality & whether NTE of FAP remain appropriate.

content.html: Objective
Evaluate effect of identified misstatements on audit & uncorrected misstatements, if any, on FS.
Accumulation of Identified Misstatements
Accumulate misstatements identified during audit, other than clearly trivial.
May designate an amount below which misstatements would be clearly trivial & wouldn't be accumulated

“Clearly trivial” is not same as “not material" [ wholly different (smaller) order of magnitude + clearly
inconsequential, individually or aggregate & judged by any criteria of size, nature or circumstances]
When any uncertainty about whether items are clearly trivial, matter considered not clearly trivial.
Difference between factual, judgmental & projected misstatements
Factual misstatements: Misstatements about which there is no doubt.
Judgmental misstatements: Differences of judgments of mgt concerning a/c estimates that auditor
finds unreasonable, or selection/application of a/c policies that auditor finds inappropriate.
Projected misstatements: Auditor's best estimate of misstatements in populations, involving projection
of misstatements in audit samples to entire populations from which samples were drawn.

Nature & circumstances of occurrence of identified misstatements indicate that other misstatements

topics.title: SA 505: External Confirmations

content.html: External confirmation: Audit evidence obtained as a direct written response to auditor from a 3°? party
(confirming party), in paper form, or by electronic or other medium.
External Confirmation Procedures ‘
When using external confirmation procedures, auditor shall maintain control over external confirmation
requests, including:
Determining info. to be confirmed or requested
Selecting appropriate confirming party
Designing confirmation requests, including determining that requests are properly addressed & contain
return info. for responses to be sent directly to auditor
Sending the requests, including follow-up requests when applicable, to confirming party.
Factors to consider when designing confirmation requests include: (Inter)
Layout & presentation of confirmation request.
Assertions being addressed.
Prior experience on the audit or similar engg.
Specific identified ROMM, including fraud risks.
Mgt's authorisation or encouragement to confirming parties to respond to auditor. Confirming parties
may be willing to respond to a confirmation request containing mgt's authorisation.
Method of communication (for eg, in paper form, or by electronic or other medium).
Ability of intended confirming party to confirm or provide requested info. (for eg, individual invoice
amount versus total balance)
Positive Confirmation Requests (PCR)
PCR asks confirming party to reply in all cases, either by indicating agreement or providing info.
Response to PCR expected to provide reliable audit evidence.
There is risk that confirming party may reply without verifying if info. is correct.
Auditor may reduce this risk by not stating amt on confirmation request & ask confirming party to fill
amount or furnish other info.
On other hand, use of this type of “blank” confirmation request may result in lower response rates
because additional effort required by confirming parties.
Negative Confirmations Request (NCR)
Request that confirming party respond directly to auditor only if confirming party disagrees with info.
provided in request. NCR provide less persuasive evidence than positive confirmations.
Auditor shall not use NCR as sole substantive audit procedure to address assessed ROMM at assertion
level unless all of following are present:

Auditor has assessed ROMM as low & obtained SAAE regarding operating effectiveness of controls
Population comprises large no. of small, homogeneous, account balances, transactions or conditions
A very low exception rate is expected &
Auditor is not aware of circumstances that would cause recipients to disregard such requests.
No response in case of Negative confirmation:
¢ Failure to receive response doesn't indicate receipt by intended confirming party of confirmation
request or verification of accuracy of info contained in request.
¢ Failure of confirming party to respond provides significantly less persuasive audit evidence than PCR.
e Also, confirming parties more likely to respond with disagreement when info. requested is not in their
favour & less likely to respond otherwise.
Non-Response
Failure of confirming party to respond, or fully respond, to PCR, or a confirmation request returned
undelivered. In such case, auditor shall perform alternate audit procedures.
Examples of alternative audit procedures auditor may perform include:
* A/c receivable balances - examining specific subsequent cash receipts, shipping documentation, &
sales near period-end.
* A/c payable balances - examining subsequent cash disbursements or correspondence from 3"4
parties, & other records, such as goods received notes.
Exception
A response that indicates a difference between info. requested to be confirmed, or contained in entity's
records, & info. provided by confirming party.
+ Auditor shall investigate exceptions to determine whether or not they are indicative of misstatement.
+ Exception needs to be assessed to entire population after analysing reason for difference.
+ Auditor's evaluation, when considered with other procedures may assist in concluding whether SAAE
been obtained or performing FAP is necessary, as per SA 330.
Mgt's Refusal to Allow the Auditor to Send a Confirmation Request

a. Inquire mgt's reasons for refusal & seek audit evidence of their validity & reasonableness
b. Evaluate implications of mgt's refusal on auditor's assessment of ROMM, including risk of fraud &
NTE of other audit procedures &
c. Perform alternative audit procedures to obtain relevant & reliable audit evidence.
v If auditor concludes mgt's refusal is unreasonable or unable to obtain relevant & reliable audit
evidence from alternative audit procedures, communicate with TCWG as per SA 260.
v Determine implications for audit & auditor's opinion as per SA 705.

As per SA 500, even when audit evidence obtained from external sources, circumstances may exist
that affect its reliability. All responses carry risk of interception, alteration or fraud. Such risk exists
regardless of whether response is obtained in paper form, or by electronic or other medium.
Factors that may indicate doubts about reliability of a response include that it:
Was received by auditor indirectly OR appeared not to come from originally intended confirming party.
Unreliable responses may indicate a fraud risk factor that requires evaluation.

topics.title: SA 510: Initial Audit Engagements - Opening Balances

content.html: Initial audit engg.: Engg. in which FS for prior period, not audited or audited by a predecessor auditor.
Opening balances: A/c balances that exist at beginning of period. Also include disclosures that existed
at beginning of period, such as contingencies & commitments.
Objective
To obtain SAAE about whether:
Opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect current period's FS
Appropriate a/c policies reflected in opening balances been consistently applied in current period's FS,
or changes properly accounted, presented & disclosed as per AFRF.
Audit Procedures: Opening Balances
Read most recent financial statements & audit report.
Obtain SAAE about whether opening balances contain material misstatements by:
Determining whether prior period's closing balances correctly brought forward or any adjustments
disclosed as prior period items in current year's P&L
Determining whether opening balances reflect application of appropriate a/c policies
Performing one or more of following audit procedures:
i) Where prior year FS were audited, perusing copies of audited FS
ii) Evaluating whether current period audit procedures provide evidence of opening balances or
iii) Performing specific audit procedures to obtain evidence regarding opening balances.
If auditor obtains audit evidence that opening balances contain misstatements that could materially
affect current period's FS, perform additional audit procedures to determine effect.
If auditor concludes misstatements exist in current period's FS, communicate with mgt & TCWG.
0) Standards on Auditing
Opening current assets & liabilities > audit evidence obtained during current audit procedures
Debtors/Creditors: Collection (payment) of opening a/c receivable (a/c payable) during current period.
. Inventories: Current period's audit procedures on closing inventory balance provide little audit evidence
regarding opening inventory.
Additional audit procedures may be necessary, & one or more of following may provide SAAE:
Observing a current physical inventory count & reconciling to opening inventory quantities.
Performing audit procedures on valuation of opening inventory items.
Performing audit procedures on gross profit & cut-off.
Consistency of A/c Policies
Obtain SAAE that A/c policies been consistently applied &
any changes been properly accounted & adequately presented & disclosed as per AFRF.
If not > Qualified/Adverse opinion as per SA 705
Conclusion & Reporting
Unable to obtain SAAE > Qualify/Disclaimer of opinion as per SA 705
Opening balance contain misstatement that materially affects current period FS & not properly
accounted & disclosed > Qualified/Adverse Opinion as per SA 705
Modification to opinion in predecessor audit report: If relevant & material to current FS, modify current
period audit report.

topics.title: SA 530 “Audit Sampling”

content.html: Objective: To provide reasonable basis to draw conclusions about population.
Audit sampling (sampling):
Application of audit procedures to less than 100% items within a population such that all sampling units
have a chance of selection to provide a reasonable basis to draw conclusions about entire population.
Sampling risk: Risk that auditor's conclusion based on sample may be different from conclusion if entire
population were subjected to same audit procedure.
Types of Sampling Risks?
Sampling risk can lead to 2 types of erroneous conclusions:
(i) In case of TOCs, controls are more effective than actual OR in case of TODs, material misstatement
does not exist when it does. Affects audit effectiveness & lead to inappropriate audit opinion.
cama 0) Standards on Auditing
(ii) In case of TOCs, controls are less effective than they actually are, OR in case of TODs, material
misstatement exists when in fact it does not. Affects audit efficiency & lead to additional work to
establish that initial conclusions were incorrect.
Non-Sampling Risk: Risk of erroneous conclusion for any reason not related to sampling risk.
Note: Detection risk comprises sampling & non-sampling risk.
Tolerable misstatement [TM]
Monetary amt set by auditor for which auditor seeks to obtain appropriate level of assurance that this
amount isn't exceeded by actual misstatement in population,
Its application of performance materiality, to a sampling procedure.
It may be same amount or amount lower than performance materiality.
Sample Design, Size & Selection of Items for Testing
i) When designing audit sample, consider purpose of audit & characteristics of population.
ii) Determine sample size sufficient to reduce sampling risk to acceptably low level.
iii) Select items in a way that each sampling unit in population has chance of selection.
Stratification & Value-Weighted Selection (Inter)
Stratification: Audit efficiency may be improved if auditor stratifies a population by dividing it into
discrete sub-populations (Stratum) having identifying characteristics.
How?
When performing TODs, population often stratified by monetary value. This allows greater effort
directed to large value items, as these items likely to be overstated,
Similarly, population may be stratified as per particular characteristic that indicates higher RoMM,
Eg, when testing provision for doubtful a/c in valuation of debtors, balances may be stratified by age.
Projection:
Results of samples drawn under each sub population are projected to that respective stratum.
Projected misstatements of each stratum combined together to consider possible effect of
misstatement in account balances & class of transactions.
Value-Weighted Selection: When performing TODs it may be efficient to identify sampling unit as
individual monetary units that make up population. Selecting specific monetary units from population.
Sample Selection Methods (Inter)
Principal methods are as follows:
Random selection (applied through random number generators, for eg, random number tables).
* Simple Random Sampling: Whole population has equal chance of selection
* Stratified Sampling: Dividing population in few groups called strata & taking samples from them.

Projecting Misstatements

Evaluating Results of Audit Sampling
Auditor shall evaluate-
a) The results of sample and
b) Whether use of audit sampling has provided reasonable basis for conclusions about the population tested.
If auditor concludes audit sampling hasn't provided reasonable basis for conclusions about population
tested, auditor may:
i. request mgt to investigate misstatements, potential for further misstatements & make adjustments
ii. tailor NTE of further audit procedures to best achieve required assurance.
Eg. in TOCs, might extend sample size, test alternative control or modify related substantive procedures.

Mgt Bias
FRFs require neutrality i.e. freedom from bias. A/c estimates can be influenced by mgt judgment.
May involve mgt bias. Unintentional & intentional mgt bias are inherent in making a/c estimate.
Mgt bias identified during previous audit influence current period risk identification & assessment.
Mgt bias is difficult to detect at a/c level. May be identified only when considered in aggregate of
groups of a/c estimates or all a/c estimates or when observed over a no. of accounting periods.
Although some mgt bias is inherent in a/c estimates, there may be no intention to mislead users of FS.
However, when there is intention to mislead, management bias is fraudulent in nature.
Measurement objective of a/c estimates
It can vary depending on AFRF & financial item.
For some a/c estimates it is to forecast outcome of transactions, events or conditions.
For others, including FV a/c estimates, it is different & expressed in terms of value of FS item based
on conditions on measurement date, such as estimated market price for asset or liability.
For eg, AFRF may require FV measurement based on assumed hypothetical current transaction between
knowledgeable, willing parties (referred as “marketplace participants” or equivalent) in an arm's length
transaction, rather than the settlement of a transaction at some past or future date.
Difference between outcome of a/c estimate & amount recognised/disclosed in FS does not necessarily
represent a misstatement. This is for FV a/c estimates, as any outcome is affected by events or
conditions subsequent to date at which its measured for FS.
Objective of SA 540
To obtain SAAE whether as per AFRF:
a/c estimates, including FV a/c estimates in FS are reasonable &
related disclosures in FS are adequate.

content.html: Objectives of Auditor
Obtain understanding of RP relationships & transactions to:
i. Recognise fraud risk factors, arising from such transactions &
ii, Conclude whether Fs:

Related party - Party that is either:
RP as defined in FRF or
Where FRF establishes minimal or no related party requirements:
a) Person or other entity that has control or significant influence, over reporting entity
b) Another entity over which reporting entity has control or significant influence or
c) Another entity that is under common control with reporting entity through having:
Common controlling ownership or Owners who are close family members or Common key mgt
Exception: Entities under common control by a state (i.e. national, regional or local govt) not considered

topics.title: SA 570: Going Concern (GC)

content.html: Going Concern Basis of Accounting
FS are prepared on assumption that entity will continue operations for foreseeable future.
General purpose FS are prepared using GC basis of accounting, unless mgt intends to liquidate entity or
cease operations or has no other realistic alternative.
Special purpose FS may or may not be prepared as per GC basis of accounting.
When GC basis is appropriate > assets & liabilities are recorded on basis that entity will be able to
realize its assets & discharge liabilities in normal course of business.
If GC not appropriate > FS prepared using liquidation basis.
Responsibilities of mgt
To assess entity's ability to continue as GC.
To make appropriate disclosures of GC in the FS.
Auditor's Responsibilities
Obtain SAAE & conclude on, appropriateness of mgt's use of GC basis of accounting
To conclude whether a material uncertainty exists about entity's ability to continue as a GC,
However, auditor cannot guarantee entity's ability to continue as a GC.

When performing RAP as per SA 315, consider whether events or conditions exist that may cast
significant doubt on entity's ability to continue as a G.C.

content.html: in Independent Auditor's Report
Applicablity: Applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose FS of listed entities & circumstances
when auditor decides to communicate KAM & required by law/regulation.
KAM are matters that in auditor's professional judgment, were of most significance in audit of FS of
current period. Selected from matters communicated with TCWG.
Objective of Auditor
To enhance communicative value of audit report by providing greater transparency about audit.
To assist user in understanding matters that, in auditor's professional judgment, were of most
significance in audit of FS of current period.
Communicating KAM is not:
A substitute for
a) disclosures in FS as per AFRF
b) auditor expressing a modified opinion as per SA 705
c) reporting as per SA 570 when a material uncertainty exists relating to events or conditions that
may cast significant doubt on an entity's ability to continue as a GC

Factors > Determining Key Audit Matters
Auditor shall determine, from matters communicated with TCWG, those matters that required
significant auditor attention. In making this determination, auditor shall take into account the following:
Areas of higher assessed RoMM or significant risks identified as per SA 315
Significant auditor judgments relating to areas in FS that involved significant mgt judgment, including
a/c estimates having high estimation uncertainty.
Effect on audit of significant events or transactions that occurred during the period.
Eg. of Key Audit Matters
Impairment Assessment, Provision for losses & contingencies, Valuation of financial instruments, Revenue
recognition, Taxation matters (multiple tax jurisdictions, uncertain tax position, deferred tax assets)
Communicating Key Audit Matters
Introductory language in this section of audit report shall state that:
KAM are those matters that, in auditor's professional judgment, which were of most significance in audit
of FS [of current period] &
These matters were addressed in context of audit of FS & forming auditor's opinion & auditor doesn't
provide separate opinion on these matters.
Can matters other than disclosed in FS be KAM?
There may be other matters communicated with TCWG that required significant auditor attention &
therefore may be determined to be KAM.
Such matters may include matters relevant to audit not required to be disclosed in FS.

content.html: Scope
Deals with auditor's responsibilities relating to other info. (financial or non-financial) contained in Annual
Report.
Auditor's opinion on FS doesn't cover other info. (Annual Report)
He's just required to read & consider other info. for any materially inconsistent info. from FS that may
indicate MM in either FS or Annual Report
Auditor's responsibility apply whether other info. is received prior to or after auditor's report
Note: This SA doesn't apply to preliminary announcements of financial info. or prospectus.
Obtaining the Other Information
Determine, through discussion with mgt, which document(s) comprises annual report & entity's planned
manner & timing of issuance of such document(s)
Make arrangements with mgt to obtain in timely manner &, if possible, prior to date of audit report, final
version of annual report &
When annual report not available until the date of audit report, request mgt to provide a WR that final
version of document(s) will be provided to auditor when available & prior to its issuance by entity, such
that auditor can complete procedures required by this SA.
01 Standards on Auditing
Reading & Considering the Other Information
Auditor shall read the other info & shall:
Consider whether there is material inconsistency between
e other info. & FS &
e other info. & auditor's knowledge obtained in audit.
While reading other info, remain alert for indications that other info may be materially misstated.
Responding when Material Inconsistency Appears to Exist or
Other Info. Appears to be Materially Misstated
Discuss the matter with mgt &, if necessary, perform other procedures to conclude whether:
a. A material misstatement of other info. exists
b, A material misstatement of FS exists or
c. Auditor's understanding of entity & its environment needs to be updated.
When other info. is materially misstated
Request mgt to correct other info > if mgt:
a) Agrees to make correction, determine that correction made OR

Tf auditor concludes MM exists in other info. obtained prior to date of auditor's report, & other info.

a) Considering implications for auditor's report & communicating with TCWG about how auditor plans to
address the MM in auditor's report OR
b) Withdrawing from engg, where withdrawal possible under applicable L/R.
Tf auditor concludes that MM exists in other info. obtained after date of audit report:
a, If other info. is corrected, perform necessary procedures OR
b. If other info. isn't corrected after communicating with TCWG, take appropriate action considering
auditor's legal rights & obligations, to bring uncorrected MM to attention of users.
When FS are materially misstated or Auditor's understanding needs to be updated
Respond as per other SAs.

Penalty for Falsely Claiming to be a Member
Sec 24 provides that any person who-
not being a member of ICAI > represents that he's member of ICAT or uses designation CA
being a member of ICAT, but not having COP, represents he's in practice or practice as a CA,
punishable on 1st conviction with fine upto 1000 & on subsequent conviction with imprisonment upto

Significance of Certificate of Practice
As per Section 6 of CA Act, 1949:-
No member of ICAT shall practice in India or elsewhere unless obtained from Council a COP.
Every such member shall pay annual fee.
COP may be cancelled by Council under prescribed circumstances.
Note: Member not in practice can't accept engagement to render services of any type normally
prescribed for a CA, even though he does not require special qualifications for doing so.
A CAiP suspended from practice for 6 months & surrendered his COP. During period of suspension,
member did not undertake any audit assignments, he undertook representation assignments for income
tax whereby he would appear before tax authorities in his capacity as a CA.
CA not holding COP can't take any other work because it would be violation of CA Act, 1949.
e If member is suspended & not holding COP, he cannot in any other capacity take up any practice
separable from his capacity to practice as a member of ICAT.
° This is because once a person becomes a CA, he's bound by CA Act, 1949 & its Regulations.
e He cannot set Regulations at naught by contending, he's entitled to practice in some other capacity.
e If he appears before tax authorities, he is doing so only in his capacity as CA & member of ICAI.
Conclusion: CA would not be allowed to represent before income tax authorities for period he remains

Audit risk components
Inherent Risk
Susceptibility of assertion to misstatement that could be material, assuming there are no related
controls. It is addressed at both FS & assertion level.
Eg. technological developments making product obsolete, causing inventory susceptible to overstatement.
Arise from entity's size, operations, complexity, objectives & regulatory environment.
Risks of particular concern to auditor might include:
Lack of working capital to continue operations | A/c estimates with high measurement uncertainty
Complex calculations which could be misstated | Declining Industry with many business failures
High value inventory
. Control Risk (Do internal controls in place mitigate inherent risk)
Risk that IC system will not prevent, or detect & correct material misstatement ona timely basis.
Entity level controls like board oversight, IT general controls & HR policies are pervasive to all assertions
whereas activity level controls relate to specific assertions.
Some control risk will always exist because of inherent limitations of IC.
Understand IC & assess RoMM at assertion level.
. Detection Risk
Risk that auditor will not detect a material misstatement.
Acceptable level of detection risk for given level of audit risk bears inverse relationship to ROMM.
In designing & evaluating results procedures, consider possibility of:
v Selecting inappropriate audit procedure,
vy Misapplying appropriate audit procedure or
y Misinterpreting the results from audit procedure.
Audit Risk = RoMM * Detection Risk
RoMM = Risk that MM may exist in FS before start of audit i.e Inherent Risk * Control risk

NBFC classification based on 4 layers based on their size, activity & riskiness.
Base Layer shall comprise of
non-deposit taking NBFCs below asset size of 21000 cr &
NBFCs undertaking following activities- .
NBFC Peer to Peer Lending (NBFC-P2P) Non-Operative Financial Holding Co. (NOFHC)
NBFC-Account Aggregator (NBFC-AA) NBFCs not availing public funds & no customer interface

Core >> Standalone >> Housing >> Infrastructure [Debt fund/finance cos]
Eg. if Housing finance Co. has asset size of 7800 Cr >> covered in middle layer. Asset size doesn't matter.
Upper Layer: NBFCs specifically identified by RBI based on a set of parameters & scoring methodology.
Top 10 eligible NBFCs in terms of asset size always in upper layer, irrespective of any other factor.
Top Layer: Ideally empty. Can get populated if RBI is of opinion that there's substantial increase in
potential systemic risk in NBFCs in Upper Layer. Such NBFCs shall move to Top from Upper Layer.
Categorisation of NBFCs carrying out specific activity
NBFC-P2P, AA, NOFHC & NBFCs w/o public funds & customer interface will always remain in Base Layer.
NBFC-D, CIC, IFC & HFC will be included in Middle/Upper Layer (not Base layer). SPD & IDF-NBFC will
always remain in Middle Layer.
Remaining NBFCs,
Investment & Credit Cos. (NBFC-ICC), Micro Finance Institution (NBFC-MFI), NBFC-Factors &
Mortgage Guarantee Companies (NBFC-MGC) could lie in any of layers depending on parameters.
Government owned NBFCs placed in Base/Middle Layer. Not in Upper Layer.

Evaluate mgt activities & advise on improving ICs & manage risks by recommending mitigating controls.
TA is important element of mgt controlling function
v Helps mgt to set up systems & processes to mitigate risk.
v Report on identified gaps & areas of weak internal control
¥ Identify root cause of problems & suggest mitigating steps & strengthen ICs.
Conclusion: TA important function that helps mgt to achieve org. goals & work in an orderly manner.
Audit Trail
Audit Trail (or Edit Log) is visible trail of evidence for tracing info. in reports to original source.
Audit trails are chronological record of changes made to data. Any change i.e. creating, updating or
deleting data must be recorded.
Records maintained as audit trail may include following info.:
when changes were made i.e., date & time (timestamp)
who made the change i.e., User Id
what data was changed i.e., data/transaction reference; success/failure
To demonstrate that audit trail feature was functional, operated & not disabled, Co. would have to design
& implement specific ICs which would be evaluated by auditors, as appropriate.
Illustrative list of controls to be implemented & operated are given below:
Controls to ensure that:
audit trail feature hasn't been disabled or deactivated
access to audit trail (& backups) is disabled/restricted & access logs are maintained.
changes to configurations of audit trail are authorized & logs of such changes are maintained,
User IDs are assigned to each individual & User IDs are not shared
periodic backups of audit trails taken & archived as per statutory period.

Difference between DD & Audit
DD is different from audit. Audit is independent examination of FS of organization to express opinion.
e DD refers to examination of potential investment to confirm all material facts of prospective business

° DD is the care a reasonable person should take before entering into agreement with another party.

Forensic professional is often involved in:
1. Fraud Detection: Investigating & analyzing financial evidence, detecting financial frauds & tracing
misappropriated funds.
2. Computer Forensics: Developing computerized applications to assist in recovery, analysis & presentation
of financial evidence.
3. Fraud Prevention: Either reviewing ICs to verify adequacy or consultation in development &
implementation of ICs as per organization's risk profile.
4. Providing Expert Testimony: Assisting in legal proceedings, including testifying in court as expert witness
and preparing visual aids to support trial evidence.
Process of Forensic Accounting
1. Initialization:
Y Clarify & remove all doubts as to real motive, purpose & utility of assignment.
v Helpful to meet client to understand important facts, players & issues.
v Conflict check should be carried out as soon as relevant parties established.
Y Preliminary investigation allows planning based on a more complete understanding of issues.

Investigating team should be skilled in collecting evidence to be used in a court case within stipulated

Tf evidence is inconclusive or there are gaps in chain of custody, evidence may be challenged in court
or become inadmissible.
Be alert to documents being falsified, damaged or destroyed by the suspect(s).
4. Perform the analysis:
Actual analysis performed will depend upon nature of assignment & may involve:
v calculating economic damages

¥ performing a regression/sensitivity analysis
5. Reporting
v Final step of forensic accounting. Include info. about fraudulent activity, if any found.
v Report findings, evidence, conclusion of amount of loss & identify those involved in fraud.
¥ May include sections on nature of assignment, scope, approach, limitations & findings &/or opinions.
v Include schedules & graphics to support & explain findings.
v Discuss how fraudster set up fraud scheme & controls, if any, were circumvented.
v¥ Recommend improvements to controls to prevent similar frauds in future.

One engg. may include multiple assignments, multiple reports may be issued; one for each assignment.

topics.title: SA 810 - Engg. to Report on Summary FS

content.html: What do Summary FS Reflect?
Summary FS reflect historical financial info. derived from FS, but contains less detail than FS while
providing structured representation consistent with FS of entity's economic resources or obligations at
a point in time or changes therein for a period of time.
Engagement Acceptance
Auditor shall, ordinarily, accept engg. to report on summary FS only when engaged to conduct audit as
per SAs of FS from which summary FS are derived.
Tf auditor has not audited FS from which summary FS are derived, auditor shall not have necessary
knowledge to discharge responsibilities in relation to summary FS as per this SA.
Before accepting engg. to report on summary FS, auditor shall:
Determine whether applied criteria are acceptable.
Applied criteria means criteria applied by mgt in preparation of summary FS.
Mgt is responsible for determining info. to be reflected in summary FS so that they are consistent, in
all material respects, or represent fair summary of audited FS.
Because summary FS contain aggregated info. & limited disclosure, there is increased risk that they may
be misleading in circumstances.
This risk increases when established criteria for preparation of summary FS do not exist.
Factors affecting auditor's determination of acceptability of applied criteria:
Nature of entity
Purpose of the summary FS.
Info. needs of intended users of summary F.S. &
Whether applied criteria will result in summary FS that are not misleading.
Presumption: Criteria for preparation of summary FS may be established by standards setting
organisation or L/R. Auditor may presume that such criteria are acceptable. Where established criteria
don't exist, criteria may be developed by mgt, for eg, based on practice in a particular industry.
If applied criteria is unacceptable:
Tf auditor concludes applied criteria is unacceptable or unable to obtain agreement of mgt, not accept
engg. to report on summary FS, unless required by L/R.
Engg. conducted as per such L/R doesn't comply with this SA.
A/R on summary FS shall not indicate engg. was conducted as per this SA.
Include appropriate reference to this fact in terms of engg.
Also determine its effect on engg. to audit FS from which summary FS are derived,
Adequate disclosure of summarised nature of summary FS & identity of audited FS be provided by title
such as "Summary FS prepared from audited FS for year ended March 31, 20XX"

Limited assurance is obtained where engg. risk is reduced to a level acceptable in circumstances of engg.,

SAE 3400 - Examination of Prospective Financial Info. (PFI)

content.html: Examine & report on PFI including examination procedures for best-estimate & hypothetical assumptions.
Note:
Need not necessarily be performed by stat. auditor of entity's FS.
This SAE does not apply to examination of PFI expressed in general/narrative terms, such as mgt's
discussion & analysis in annual report.
What is Prospective financial information (PFI)?
PFT is financial info based on:
Assumptions about events that may occur in the future &
Possible actions by entity.
Prospective financial info can be in form of forecast, projection, or combination of both.
Eg. 1-year forecast plus 5-year projection.
What is Forecast?
PFI prepared on the basis of assumptions of
future events which mgt expects &
Actions mgt expects to take on date PFI is prepared.
Best estimate assumptions- assumption that reflects anticipated experience with no provision for risk
of adverse deviation.
Eg. In present market conditions, supply availability, historical buying patterns & seasonal trends, CFO
expects sales to increase by 5% in next quarter. Therefore, 5% sales increase is his financial forecast.
12.1
12 SAE
What is Projection?
PFI prepared on basis of:
Hypothetical assumptions about
vy future events & mgt actions
¥ not necessarily expected to take place
Eg entities in start-up phase or considering major change in nature of operations or
Mixture of best-estimate & hypothetical assumptions (imagined or suggested)
Examples:
1. X Ltd may project a course of action to take when one or more hypothetical situations arise, such as
creating a new product to meet demand of expected market growth.
2. Co. plans to raise funds from a prospective equity investor & has asked a firm of CAs to examine profit
forecast for placing it before prospective equity investor.
3. Co. is in process of setting up new plant. Needs loan from bank. Prepared a projection of its profits,
cash flows for next 7 years along with assumptions.
Nature of Assurance Regarding PFI
PFI relates to events & actions that have not occurred & might not occur. While evidence may be available
to support assumptions, such evidence is generally future- oriented & speculative. Therefore, opinion as
to whether results shown in PFI will be achieved cannot be expressed.

Can Professional Accountants be associated with PFI?
Clause 3 of Part I of Second Schedule to CA Act, 1949 states CAiP shall be deemed to be guilty of Prof.
Misconduct, if he permits his or firm's name to be used in connection with EOE contingent upon future
transactions in a manner which may lead to belief that he vouches for accuracy of forecast.
CA can prepare profit/financial forecasts & review them, clearly indicating in report:
Sources of info, Basis of forecasts & major Assumptions & doesn't vouch for accuracy of forecasts.
Also applies to projections made on basis of hypothetical assumptions about future events & mgt actions
not necessarily expected to take place so long as vouching for accuracy isn't made.
Duties of Member Examining PFI
Auditor should obtain SAAE as to whether:
. Mgt's best-estimate assumptions are not unreasonable & hypothetical assumptions are consistent with
purpose of info.

content.html: Compilation of Pro Forma Financial Information (PFFI) Included in a Prospectus
What is Pro forma financial information (PFFI)?
PFFI refers to financial info. shown with adjustments to illustrate
Y impact of event or transaction

content.html: Not all engagements performed by practitioners are assurance engagements.
Other frequently performed engg. that are not assurance engg. include:-
Preparation of tax returns where no assurance is expressed.
Consulting (or advisory) engg. such as mgt & tax consulting.
Engg. covered by SRS, such as agreed-upon procedures engg. & compilations of financial or other info.
What are Agreed-upon Procedures?
Auditor is engaged to issue a report of factual findings, based on
specified procedures performed
on specified subject matter
of specified elements, a/cs or items of a FS.
Eg. Perform certain procedures on individual items of FS, say, a/c payable, a/c receivable, RP purchases
& sales & profits of a segment, or a FS, say, a BS or even complete set of FS.
However, person performing related services need not necessarily be auditor of entity's FS.

topics.title: SRS 4400 Engg. to Perform Agreed Upon Procedure regarding Financial Info.

content.html: Objective
Carry out procedures of audit nature to which auditor & entity & any appropriate 3" parties have agreed
& report on factual findings.
No assurance is provided.
Users of report assess procedures & findings & draw their own conclusions.
Report is usually restricted to parties that have agreed to procedures to be performed since others,
unaware of reasons for procedures, may misinterpret the results.
Summary: No assurance is provided in such a report. These are non-assurance engg.
Audit Vs. Agreed-upon Procedures (AUP)
Key difference between audit & AUP relates to assurance.
Audit expresses opinion & provides assurance to users.
However, in AUP, only report of factual findings provided. No assurance is given to users.
Instead, users draw own conclusions based on factual findings in report.
For eg, AUP engg. to evaluate validity of a/c payable may state following:
¥ Comparing names of major suppliers & o/s amounts as on date to names & amounts in trial balance.

Sustainability reporting & its expected benefits
Practice of reporting publicly economic, environmental, and/or social impacts & contributions (positive
or negative) towards sustainable development.
Info that companies provide about performance to outside world on regular basis in structured way.
Expected Benefits:
Understand performance: Help stakeholders to understand organizations performance vis a vis
sustainability & impacts. Reporting process links financial & non-financial performance.
Long term value: Such reporting can help entities to focus on long-term value creation, by addressing
environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues.
Investing: Investors are increasingly recognising environmental & social issues provide both risks &
opportunities in respect of investments & seeking disclosures on environmental & social performance of
businesses, they can use ESG performance to make investment decisions,
Three pillars constitute ESG
- Environment (E): Environmental stands for corporate climate policies, energy use, waste, pollutions,
natural resource conservation & treatment of animals. Includes natural resources that every entity
uses like coal, water etc.
Social (S): Addresses relationships & reputation with people & institutions. Also includes labour
relations, diversity & inclusions.
Governance (6): It is ICs & procedures entity adopts to govern, make effective investment decisions,
comply with law & meet needs of stakeholders,
ESG Reporting:
ESG reporting disclose info, data, metrics that explain value added in these 3 areas.
It can be both quantitative & qualitative in nature.
Qualitative reports describe Co's strategy or policy & Quantitative approach includes metrics & KPIs
to measure progress against goals & report achievements.
Mixed approach that uses both qualitative & quantitative info adds to quality of disclosures.

Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR)
Top 1000 listed companies by market capitalization required to file BRSR.
Reporting questionnaire is divided into 3 sections:
i) Section A - General Disclosures
Details of listed cos., products, services, operations, employee details, holding, subsidiary, associate co.
ii) Section B - Management Process and disclosures
Questions related to policy & mgt processes, governance, leadership, & oversight.
iii) Section C - Principle-wise performance disclosures
Report upon Key performance indicators (KPIs) in alignment with 9 principles of NGRBC
[National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct]
The section classifies KPIs into 2 categories that companies are required to report upon:
- Essential indicators (Mandatory disclosures)
Data on training programs, environmental data on energy, emissions, water, waste mgt etc.
- Leadership indicators (Optional disclosures)
Life cycle assessments, conflict mgt policy, additional data on biodiversity, energy consumptions, supply
chain mgt etc.

9 principles in BRSR are categorized into ESG components of Environment, Social & Governance with 2

Principle 1 - Ethics, Transparency & Accountability (EAT)
Emphasizes that business decisions should be open to disclosure & accessible to relevant parties.
Core elements:
Policies: Entities’ governing structure should develop policies, procedures & practices for their offices,
factories & work areas, ensuring ethics is not compromised.
Share with stakeholders: Info. of policies, procedures & practices with performance should be made
available to stakeholders,
Adverse effects: For adverse effects, care has to be taken for transparent disclosures.

Principle 2 - Safe & Sustainable Goods & Service
Make sure that goods, services & operations result in better life for consumers & end-users.
Core elements:
Minimise Resources: Product design, production methods & technologies should minimize resource usage.
. Spread Awareness: Entities to educate & make consumers & clients aware about their rights.
RRR: Take measures that reduce over exploitation of nature's resources by consuming sustainably &
encourage methods for reduce, reuse & recycling of resources.
Principle 3 - Promote well-being of all employees including those in value chain
Initiatives entity takes for benefit of its employees dignity, health, well-being.
Core elements:
Compliance: Ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements as far as employees are concerned.
Dignity & Freedom: Respect dignity of employee as human being & shouldn't restrict their freedom of
associations, unions for collective bargaining of rights & redressal of issues.
Child Labour: Prevent child labour, bonded labour & other forms of involuntary labour.
Work life Balance: Have system in which work-life balance is not compromised.
Timely Payment: Ensure timely payment of worker's wages & compensation.
Living wages: Payment of wages as per living wages, considering basic needs & provide economic security.
Harassment free: Creation of workplace free of harassment & violence.

Principle 4 - Respect for stakeholders’ interests & responsiveness
Concept of interested party or stakeholders to a business has been a point of discussion in all regulatory
& voluntary systems that relate to mgt system of any organisation, be it related to quality, environment
or occupational health & safety of workers.
Core elements:
Disclose Impact: Be transparent & communicate with stakeholders about impacts of operations &
decisions on people & nature. Policies, decisions & impact of operations have to be disclosed
transparently with no ambiguity on extent of issues.
. Determine Context: Determine context of operation & identify interested parties.
Share Benefits: Fairly share benefits to stakeholders or give opportunity to them to benefit from
operations in equitable manner.
Principle 5 - Respect & promote human rights
Covers a variety of violence & belligerent abusive issues faced by people. Refers to human rights issues
that happen directly or indirectly due to operation of business.
Core elements:
Understanding: Have clear understanding of human rights & ways by which human rights can be violated
from perspective of Constitution of India, national laws & International Bill of Human Rights.
. Mgt Systems: When developing mgt systems, integrate human rights element into policies, procedures
& practices.
Respect all: Recognize & respect human rights of all stakeholders & groups, including communities,
consumers & vulnerable & marginalized groups.
Principle 6 - Protection & restoration of Environment
Looks at environmental responsibility as a basic requirement for economic prosperity & sustainability.
Core elements:
Policies: Have policies, procedures & practices to assess & rectify impacts to environment. This should
cover whole life cycle of product.
. Optimum use: Make use of natural & manmade resources in optimum manner to ensure sustainability.
Measure performance: Measure their performance relating to prevention of pollution, destruction of
forests, waste generation, energy use, land use, etc.
. Climate change initiatives: Contribute towards climate change resilience supporting India's commitment
to international mechanisms like Paris Agreement & National Action Plans.
Best practices: Explore comparison of its activities with industry best practices to reduce, reuse &
recycle/ recover materials, resources.

Principle 7 - Influence on Public & Regulatory Policy
Positively recognizes that businesses operate within the framework of statutory & legislative policies
of governing authority.
Principle further highlights that -
a. Org. should contribute to policy formulation & policy advocacy.
b. Collective associations such as, trade groups & industry chambers to be utilized when moving ahead
with policy advocacy & formulation.
c. Role in policy advocacy by organisation should be in such a way that it encourages fair competition &

Principle 8 - Promote Inclusive Growth & equitable development
This can work only with close participation & collaboration amongst entities, authorities, civil
associations contributing to one another for a better livelihood, & assistance to marginalized
communities.
Core elements of the eighth principle are:
a. Systems: Have systems to identify & address impacts of activities on social, cultural, & economic
aspects of people. This includes business created issues like, land acquisition, use & construction
activities for new facilities.
b. Adverse impacts: Review, measure & track adverse impacts of their activities on society & environment
& make action plans to mitigate them adequately.
c. Creativity: Make efforts to bring up creative products, technologies & business concerns that help
marginalized communities to have well-being & better quality of life.
d. CSR: When designing CSR activities review local & regional development priorities to help marginalized
groups & communities.
e. Displacement of Communities: Ensure that displacement or relocation of communities doesn't happen &
in unavoidable cases, provide fair compensation to affected people.
Principle 9 ~ Provide value to consumers in responsible manner
Primary purpose of business is to create or provide useful products & services to customer for
reasonable profits.
Core elements associated with the principle are:
a. Reduce Negative Impact: Put in efforts to reduce negative impacts of products & services on
consumers, natural environment & society.
b. Freedom of choice: When conceptualizing, designing & marketing their products, org shouldn't prevent
freedom of choice & fair competition.
c. Transparency: Transparently & accurately disclose all kinds of adverse impacts to user, planet, society,
on biodiversity from their products.

Cyber Attacks
Cyber-attack is an attempt to gain unauthorized access to computing system or network with intent to
cause damage, steal, expose, alter, disable, or destroy data.
Most common types of cyberattacks are:
Malware: Malware or malicious software is any program or code created with intent to harm a computer,
network or server.
Types:
1, Ransomware: Adversary encrypts victim's data & offers to provide decryption key for payment.
2. Fileless Malware
A malicious activity that uses native, legitimate tools built into a system to execute a cyber-attack.
Unlike traditional malware, fileless malware doesn't require an attacker to install any code ona target's
system, making it hard to detect.
3. Trojan
It's a malware that appears to be legitimate software disguised as native operating system programs
or harmless files like free downloads.
4. Mobile Malware
Type of malware designed to target mobile devices, Its delivered through malicious downloads,
operating System vulnerabilities, phishing, smishing, & use of unsecured Wi-Fi.
Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack is a malicious, targeted attack that floods a network with false requests
to disrupt business operations.
© Ina DoS attack, users are unable to perform routine & necessary tasks, such as accessing email,
websites, online a/cs or other resources that are operated by a compromised computer or network.
o While most DoS attacks don't result in lost data & typically resolved without paying a ransom, they cost
organization time, money & other resources to restore critical business operations.
PHISHING is a type of cyberattack that uses email, SMS, phone, social media, & social engineering
techniques to entice a victim to share sensitive info. — such as passwords or a/c nos. — or download a
malicious file that will install viruses on their computer or phone.
Types:
1. Spear Phishing targets specific individuals or organizations through malicious emails. Goal is to steal
sensitive info such as login credentials or infect targets’ device with malware.
2. Whaling is a social engineering attack specifically targeting senior or C-level executive employees for
stealing money or info. or gaining access to person's computer to execute further cyberattacks.
3. Smishing is a fraudulent practice of sending text messages purporting to be from reputable Cos to
induce individuals to reveal personal info, eg. passwords or credit card nos.

4. Vishing, a voice phishing attack, fraudulent use of phone calls & voice messages pretending to be from
a reputable org. to convince individuals to reveal pvt info such as bank details and passwords.
SPOOFING is a technique through which cybercriminal disguises themselves as known or trusted
source, Adversary is able to engage with the target & access their systems or devices with ultimate
goal of stealing info, extorting money or installing malware or other harmful software on the device.
Types:
1. Domain Spoofing is a form of phishing where attacker impersonates a known business or person with
fake website or email domain to fool people into trusting them. Typically, domain appears to be
legitimate at 1%* glance, but closer look reveal subtle differences.
2. Email Spoofing is a type of cyberattack that targets businesses by using emails with forged sender
addresses, Because recipient trusts alleged sender, they are more likely to open the email and interact
with its contents, such as a malicious link or attachment.
Identity-Based Attacks: When a valid user's credentials been compromised & adversary pretend to be
that user. For eg, people use same user ID & password across multiple accounts. Therefore, possessing
credentials for one account may be able to grant access to other, unrelated account.
Insider Threats: When current or former employees that pose danger to an org. because they have
direct access to Co. network, sensitive data, and intellectual property (IP), as well as knowledge of
business processes, company policies or other info. that would help carry out such an attack.
DNS Tunneling is a type of cyberattack that leverages domain name system (DNS) queries & responses
to bypass traditional security measures & transmit data & code within network.
This tunnel gives hacker a route to unleash malware & extract data, IP or other sensitive info. by
encoding it bit by bit in a series of DNS responses.
IoT-Based Attack is any cyberattack that targets an Internet of Things (IoT) device or network. Once
compromised, hacker can take control of device, steal data, or join a group of infected devices

Control Considerations or Objectives of Auditing Digitally
Emerging technologies can bring great benefits, but also come with varied set of substantial risks.
As they address challenge of assessing technology risk, auditors can & should focus on following control
considerations:
1. Auditors should gain holistic understanding of changes in industry & IT environment to effectively
evaluate mgt’s process for initiating, processing, & recording transactions & then design appropriate
auditing procedures.
2. Auditors should consider risks resulting from implementation of new technologies & how those risks
may differ from those that arise from more traditional, legacy systems.
3. Consider whether digital upskilling or specialists are necessary to determine impact of new technologies
& assist in risk assessment & understanding of design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of
controls. Eg, cybersecurity control experts, IT specialists in team etc.
